`df` shows **63G/73G (87%)** used, but all visible writable directories total only **~1.2G**. The bulk of the 63G resides in the **read-only overlay image layers** (`/usr`, system libs) — these are **NOT deletable** without breaking the container. Cleanup can only reclaim space in writable dirs.

**Realistically reclaimable: ~315M** (mostly npm cache).

---

## Safety Assessment per Candidate

### 1. 🟢 NPM Cache — `/root/.npm/_cacache` (312M) — **SAFE**
Pure download cache; verified via `npm cache verify`. Regenerated on demand.

### 2. 🟢 Node compile cache — `/tmp/node-compile-cache` (2.6M) — **SAFE**
Runtime optimization cache; recreated automatically by Node.

### 3. 🟢 Orphaned `.so` files in `/tmp` (11M, 2 files) — **CAUTIOUS→SAFE**
Hidden compiled `.so` artifacts (`.bcd9f77fbc85be6d...so`). Two near-identical timestamps; appear to be JIT cache from a prior run. Safe to remove when no process uses them.

### 4. 🟢 APT archives — `/var/cache/apt/archives` (8K) — **SAFE (trivial)**
No `.deb` files present; nothing to clean.

### 5. 🟡 Logs `/var/log` (232K) — **CAUTIOUS**
Already small & logrotate is properly configured (`monthly`, `rotate 12`, `compress`). **Not worth touching** — risk > reward.

### 6. 🟡 `/var/backups` (4K) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
System-managed (`dpkg.status`, `passwd`/`group` snapshots). Essential for recovery.

### 7. 🔴 NVM/Node v22.23.2 (548M) — **RISKY**
The **only** Node version installed and **in active use** (this opencode session runs on it). Deleting breaks everything.

### 8. 🔴 `/usr` overlay (237M+) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
Read-only image layer. Removing breaks OS.

### 9. 🔴 `/logs/agent/opencode` (4.7M) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
Active opencode runtime state + DB (`opencode.db`, WAL, locks). Deleting corrupts the current session.

---

|-----|--------|-------|------|
| 1 | Clear npm cache | 312M | SAFE |
| 2 | Clear /tmp compile cache + orphan .so | ~14M | SAFE |

|------|--------|
| `/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2` | Only Node runtime; active session depends on it |

I have all the information I need. Note the key finding: `df` reports 63G used but only ~1.2G is visible in writable dirs — the bulk lives in the read-only overlay image layers (not safely deletable). Here is my analysis.

---

# System Cleanup Analysis

## ⚠️ Key Finding (Read First)

`df` shows **63G/73G (87%)** used, but all visible writable directories total only **~1.2G**. The bulk of the 63G resides in the **read-only overlay image layers** (`/usr`, system libs) — these are **NOT deletable** without breaking the container. Cleanup can only reclaim space in writable dirs.

**Realistically reclaimable: ~315M** (mostly npm cache).

---

## Safety Assessment per Candidate

### 1. 🟢 NPM Cache — `/root/.npm/_cacache` (312M) — **SAFE**
Pure download cache; verified via `npm cache verify`. Regenerated on demand.

### 2. 🟢 Node compile cache — `/tmp/node-compile-cache` (2.6M) — **SAFE**
Runtime optimization cache; recreated automatically by Node.

### 3. 🟢 Orphaned `.so` files in `/tmp` (11M, 2 files) — **CAUTIOUS→SAFE**
Hidden compiled `.so` artifacts (`.bcd9f77fbc85be6d...so`). Two near-identical timestamps; appear to be JIT cache from a prior run. Safe to remove when no process uses them.

### 4. 🟢 APT archives — `/var/cache/apt/archives` (8K) — **SAFE (trivial)**
No `.deb` files present; nothing to clean.

### 5. 🟡 Logs `/var/log` (232K) — **CAUTIOUS**
Already small & logrotate is properly configured (`monthly`, `rotate 12`, `compress`). **Not worth touching** — risk > reward.

### 6. 🟡 `/var/backups` (4K) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
System-managed (`dpkg.status`, `passwd`/`group` snapshots). Essential for recovery.

### 7. 🔴 NVM/Node v22.23.2 (548M) — **RISKY**
The **only** Node version installed and **in active use** (this opencode session runs on it). Deleting breaks everything.

### 8. 🔴 `/usr` overlay (237M+) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
Read-only image layer. Removing breaks OS.

### 9. 🔴 `/logs/agent/opencode` (4.7M) — **DO NOT TOUCH**
Active opencode runtime state + DB (`opencode.db`, WAL, locks). Deleting corrupts the current session.

---

## Priority Ranking

| Pri | Action | Space | Risk |
|-----|--------|-------|------|
| 1 | Clear npm cache | 312M | SAFE |
| 2 | Clear /tmp compile cache + orphan .so | ~14M | SAFE |
| 3 | APT autoclean | trivial | SAFE |

**Total safe reclaim: ~326M.**

---

## Specific Commands (Safe Execution)

```bash
# P1 — npm cache (312M) — safe, regenerated on demand
npm cache clean --force

# P2a — Node compile cache (2.6M)
rm -rf /tmp/node-compile-cache

# P2b — Orphaned .so artifacts in /tmp (~11M) — verify no usage first
lsof +D /tmp 2>/dev/null | grep '\.so'   # should return nothing
rm -f /tmp/.*-00000000.so

# P3 — APT (trivial, hygiene)
apt-get autoclean && apt-get autoremove --yes
```

---

## ⛔ What NOT to Delete

| Path | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2` | Only Node runtime; active session depends on it |
| `/usr`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/local` | Read-only image layer — breaks OS |
| `/var/backups` | System recovery snapshots (dpkg status) |
| `/logs/agent/opencode/` | **Active** opencode DB, WAL, locks — corrupts this session |
| `/var/log/*.log` | Logrotate already handles; small + useful for forensics |
| `/root/.config/opencode`, `/root/.local` | Active config |

---

## Process Safety Check

No processes were listable via `ps` (sandbox-restricted) and no listening ports were visible. Since nothing in the cleanup list touches active services, **it is safe to proceed**. The `.so` removal step includes an `lsof` guard as an extra precaution.

**Bottom line:** This system is already very lean in writable space. The 87% disk usage is almost entirely the base image — cleanup will only recover ~326M. If you need significantly more space, the lever is rebuilding the image with a smaller base, not runtime cleanup.
